result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Gaussian]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Gaussian (Normal) family with identity link. twitter-card: title: >- [Gaussian]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Gaussian (Normal) family with identity link. title: "[Gaussian]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Gaussian (Normal) family with identity link. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Gaussian (Normal) family with identity link. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian.py#L11-L233){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature Gaussian() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Gaussian family models a continuous, unbounded response with constant variance. It is the default family in Whittaker and corresponds to classical (penalized) least-squares regression: with the identity link, P-IRLS converges in a single step since the working response and weights do not depend on the current fit. Use it whenever the response is real-valued, approximately symmetric, and its spread does not depend systematically on its mean — for example, physical measurements, log-transformed sizes, or residual-like quantities. If the variance grows with the mean, or the response is a count, proportion, or strictly positive quantity, consider `Poisson`, `Binomial`, `Gamma`, or another family instead. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The canonical (and only supported) link is the identity function: $$ g(\mu) = \mu $$ so the linear predictor `eta` is directly on the response scale and no back-transformation is needed for predictions. The variance function is constant in the mean, $$ V(\mu) = 1, \qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y) = \phi \, V(\mu) = \sigma^2, $$ which is what makes the Gaussian family the special case in which ordinary least squares and maximum-likelihood estimation coincide. The deviance is the residual sum of squares: $$ D(y, \hat\mu) = \sum_i (y_i - \hat\mu_i)^2 . $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM with a smooth term to noisy sine-wave data using the (default) Gaussian family: ::: {#2075bef8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 200 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) y = np.sin(x) + rng.normal(0, 0.3, n) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Gaussian()) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Gaussian(link='identity') Inference: REML Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err t value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.0046 0.0205 0.224 0.8233 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 7.31 8 1279.244 < 1e-16 Total EDF: 8.31 Scale est: 0.083835 Deviance: 16.0702 Null dev: 123.9418 Dev. expl: 87.0% GCV score: 0.087470 AIC: 80.11 BIC: 107.52 ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [deviance()](#deviance){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Total deviance: the (weighted) residual sum of squares $\sum_i (y_i - \hat\mu_i)^2$. | | [initialize()](#initialize){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Starting values for `mu`: a copy of the observed response `y`. | | [link()](#link){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Apply the identity link: $\eta = \mu$. | | [link_derivative()](#link_derivative){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Derivative of the identity link: $g'(\mu) = 1$. | | [link_inverse()](#link_inverse){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Apply the inverse identity link: $\mu = \eta$. | | [log_likelihood()](#log_likelihood){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Gaussian log-likelihood evaluated at variance `scale`. | | [simulate()](#simulate){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Simulate Gaussian response values `N(mu, scale)`. | | [variance()](#variance){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Constant variance function: $V(\mu) = 1$. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total deviance: the (weighted) residual sum of squares $\sum_i (y_i - [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total log-likelihood. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate Gaussian response values `N(mu, scale)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/gaussian.py#L195-L212){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature simulate( mu, scale, rng, ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean (fitted values), shape `(n,)`.
